recipes.name: German Chocolate Cake Frosting II
ingredients_raw: 3 egg yolk, beaten with 1 teaspoon water

steps.text: In a large saucepan combine evaporated milk, sugar, egg yolks, margarine and vanilla. Cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until thick. Remove from heat and stir in pecans and coconut. Spread on cake while still warm.

raw_recipe.headline: German Chocolate Cake Frosting II
raw_recipe.description: German chocolate cake frosting that is cooked on top of the stove and put on warm cake while frosting is warm.

review.reviewBody: I made this recipe,but I added about a tablespoon/table spoon in a half of cornstarch mixed with the evaporated milk,to thicken since some people said it was a little runny.I chopped up my pecans,(only about a half cup or less)about a 1/4 cup of lightly roasted coconut.I finished making the frosting then let it sit for about an hour,it thicken up nicely but not too thick to spread.I frosted it on a nicely refrigerated german chocolate cake and it spread magnificiently.I sell cakes/pies/cookies and food and this cake was gone in 2 minutes or less I kid u not.It was a huge huge huge hit.Also to note,I never liked the frosting on the german chocolate cakes before,due to too much coconut too sweet etc... but this I added to my own liking on the coconut and pecans.It also tasted sweet when I tried it(which made me skeptical)but when it was on the cake the cake isnt that sweet mixed with the frosting it was perfect just perfect I tell u.An A+++++++++++++++++if not better.Thank you thank you thank you.

Great Recipe - FAULTY DIRECTIONS!

In some of the other recipes someone suggested using cornstarch cause the frosting was thin and drippy. Yuck! Do not use cornstarch! The problem is the level of heat. You must get the sugar to carmelize--so the mixture thickens properly. 

Bring the: evaporated milk, sugar, egg yolks, margarine and vanilla mixture to a boil...or almost boil. You can start on low heat, but unless you want to stir all day...bring the heat up until you start to see it boil. Yes, stirring constantly. Don't leave the stove! Then poor your mixture over the pecans and coconut, mix well. Cool thoroughly before using!

Oh, btw, a 12 oz can of evaporated milk is a cup and half. Maybe that is why some people said this frosting was runny? Unless you buy 8 oz cans of evaporated milk, you'll have leftover evaporated milk.

The other change I made was I added more pecans and more coconut. (I added these after I made the frosting per the measurements stated in the recipe). After testing, I wanted more coconut and pecans. The other change was: real butter, not margarine. Ask any cardiologist which is worse for your health...butter or margarine.

Loved this recipe! Way way way better than premade frosting!!! Used it on a boxed German Chocolate Cake mix w/ a Pinterest hack :) To make a bakery quality cake out of a box mix, follow these steps... 1) Add 2 extra eggs (really adds richness!) 2) Use melted butter instead of the recommended oil & double it... 3) Use milk instead of water... 4) Add 2 tsp. Pure Vanilla Extract... 5) Preheat oven to 350F, then reduce to 325F when you put the cake in :D Better for you? Um, no... But so good! Made an awesome crowd-pleasing birthday cake :)
Great advice about the corn starch. Take off heat, add pecan/coconut mixture and spread on cake before it gets too thick to spread easily. Awesome recipe

I just made this with the following tweaks:
-toasted coconut and pecans first, then added a big pinch of salt
-brought thr cooked part up at a simmer and stirred until thickened, about 7 minutes

It's thick, but spreadable, and tastes well balanced.

I made this yesterday, with my only adjustment being instead of "1cup white sugar", I used 1/2 cup white sugar plus 1/2 cup brown sugar. I did this because I saw another recipe exactly the same as this one except it called for brown sugar, so I decided to split the difference. This frosting is so delicious, I could just eat it with a spoon! It frosted a 9x13 cake just fine, but I will either double it or at least add another half recipe next time because it IS so darn declicious!!!!! A keeper!

This recipe does not need cornstarch! It just needs more detailed cooking instructions! Cook it to 220 F, and let it cool, and it's plenty thick plus delicious.
Like many, I didn't want to be there all day so I didn't do it all over low heat. Use low heat until the butter's melted, then turn it up to medium high and boil and stir it until you get to 220. Add the vanilla at that point (why boil it?) and the toasted pecans and coconut, and let it cool.

I just made this about an hour ago and it is yummy! I altered the recipe to my liking. I used half brown sugar and 1/2 regular sugar. I also altered the recipe to be able to use the whole 12 oz can of evaporated milk. So: 12 oz evaporated milk, 3/4 cup brown sugar, 3/4 cup white sugar, 4 egg yolks, 3/4 cup butter, 1 1/2 tsp. vanilla extract, 1 1/2 cups chopped pecans, and 2 cups of flaked coconut. It was enough to fill my chocolate cupcakes with some of the frosting for filling and I made a chocolate shelled border and topped with remaining coconut pecan frosting!!! Posted up a pic, you will not be disappointed so delicious!!! Happy Baking Everyone!!! :)

Used butter in place of margarine. Followed another reviewers instructions regarding cooking method - stirring continuously cooked on low for 6-7 minutes, then medium for 6-7 minutes, followed by medium-high for another 6-7 minutes. After frosting reached 200 degrees cooked an additional 2 minutes. The frosting continued to thicken while cooling. Turned out very thick without adding cornstarch. Filled and topped a 6-inch two layer cake and 14 cupcakes.
I made this recipe and loved it! I took the advise of the most helpful review by Miki and added 1 1/2 tbs cornstarch. The thickness was absolutely perfect.
Thanks for the tip to add cornstarch! I also added a couple tablespoons of brown sugar to give it a darker color. The frosting came out really good!

It's the same recipe as on the Bakers bar, except use butter. To thicken my custard after cooking it for 20 minutes, I use more coconut and pecan pieces and double the recipe because it is It's own food group.

I agree with the reviewer who said that cooking longer made a beautiful consistency frosting. I was even able to frost the sides of my cake. I just kept cooking until I could see that it was clinging well to my spatula. There was no need for cornstarch. Very yummy frosting for my birthday cake!
I am rating this recipe based on no changes. It didn’t thicken like the recipe says it should therefore it dripped off the cake.
Delicious and easy recipe to go with the German chocolate cake I made for my Dad's 93rd birthday. Everyone loved it!
So easy ... so great !!!
Excellent, not too sweet. If you're worried about the reviews that it's runny, it's because it hasn't cooked long enough. Mine took over 10 minutes but thickened up beautifuly.
was very good..

I made this recipe for my coworker who got promoted and his favorite cake is german chocolate. The icing did take long time to thicken up. Silly me accidently added a tiny amount of baking soda instead of corn starch (the containers were right next to each other :) ), but I added a pinch of flour and everything seemed to thicken up nicely. I added it into the fridge until it cooled completely just to be sure the texture came out correct and it tasted great. I went for the cornstarch before even reading the reviews and that is why I gave 4 stars. The recipe could use one more ingredient that wasn't listed.
Pleased with the amount of frosting this recipe generated. I did add a tablespoon of tapioca starch (no cornstarch on hand). My husband enjoyed his cake with this frosting!
